subject: SOC 2 applicability + CAIQ/SIG evidence request for hybrid VPC routing and tenant affinity
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightguard.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ""
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 applicability + CAIQ/SIG evidence for hybrid VPC routing and tenant affinity

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor assessment for Q4 and have a couple of follow-ups after reviewing Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and CAIQ/SIG materials. Two specific questions we'd appreciate clarity on: 

1) Does the current SOC 2 Type II report (audit period Aug 1, 2025 - Jul 31, 2026) explicitly cover Dedicated GPU pools and routing decisions that result in tenant affinity (i.e., requests pinned to a customer's dedicated capacity)? Or is the report limited to the multi-tenant hosted API only?

2) For customers using Private/VPC (customer-managed VPC connectors or on-prem variants), do CAIQ/SIG responses and any available bridge letters cover that topology, or do we need a separate attestation/evidence bundle?

If you can send a brief mapping of evidence (log types, sample retention, access controls) and a draft bridge letter we can present to our internal auditors, that would be ideal. Our audit team is short on time — can you respond by 2026-09-04?

Appreciate it,

Maria Lopez
Director, Vendor Security
BrightGuard Financial

[Attachment referenced: BG-Vendor-Questionnaire.pdf (we reviewed) ]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightguard.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability + CAIQ/SIG evidence for hybrid VPC routing and tenant affinity

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Compliance) and Ben (Infra) to provide the mapping and draft bridge letter. High-level: the SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted API and Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) where customers have committed capacity and tenant mapping is managed by Redwood. Private/VPC (customer-managed network connectors or on-prem packages) are not automatically included unless the customer elected to be in-scope during the audit period.

Kimberly / Ben — can you confirm:
- whether Dedicated pools were explicitly included for the Aug 2025–Jul 2026 report, and
- what evidence slices (log extracts, routing configs, tenant mapping docs) we can provide for BrightGuard to demonstrate isolation and controls?

Maria — we'll aim to provide a CAIQ mapping spreadsheet and a draft bridge letter by EOD 2026-09-03. If you need it sooner, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Irene

Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Safety (Sales/Partnerships Liaison)
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0172

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightguard.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability + CAIQ/SIG evidence for hybrid VPC routing and tenant affinity

Hi Maria / Irene,

Short answers up front: Dedicated (reserved) pools were in-scope for our Type II audit covering 2025-09-01 to 2026-07-31; multi-tenant hosted API was also in-scope. Private/VPC deployments were out-of-scope unless the customer consented to inclusion and we collected customer-specific evidence during the period.

What we will provide:
- CAIQ response matrix (attached) that maps CAIQ/SIG questions to Redwood artifacts for in-scope hosting modes (hosted + dedicated).
- A bridge letter template for customers using Private/VPC that describes which controls are covered by Redwood's audit and which controls are the customer's responsibility. The draft highlights limitations (network boundary, customer KMS, on-prem patching) and enumerates the evidence items a customer must supply to extend coverage.
- Evidence mapping (examples):
  * Routing and tenancy: routing config snapshots, deployment topology diagrams, tenant assignment logs (sampled), load balancer ACLs (redacted), canary/rollback policies.
  * Access controls: IAM role definition exports, RBAC assignments, short-lived credential policy docs.
  * Logging & retention: example token-level audit logs (redacted), syslog/Elk extracts for sampled requests, retention policy excerpts (retention: 365 days internal logs; 90 days surfaced to customers).

Items BrightGuard will likely need to provide (for Private/VPC in-scope requests):
- VPC peering/privatelink configuration export
- Customer-managed KMS attestation (if using customer keys)
- Evidence of network segmentation and host hardening for on-prem components

I'll attach the CAIQ matrix and the draft bridge letter. Ben — please add any infra specifics (routing TTLs, tenant affinity rules) and confirm we can produce sample logs for the audit period requested.

Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CAIQ_response_matrix_v2.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-2026_summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightguard.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability + CAIQ/SIG evidence for hybrid VPC routing and tenant affinity

Maria / team — adding infra detail.

1) Tenant affinity / routing: Dedicated pools are pinned via our scheduler and tenant assignment table; we can produce redacted assignment logs showing which tenant IDs were directed to dedicated GPUs during the audit window. For hosted-internal routing, we can provide the routing policy config and hashed, redacted request IDs.

2) Sampling & logs: We can export 30-day samples for the audit window and a 1% hashed-request sample for the full period if BrightGuard needs longitudinal proof. Logs include timestamp, hashed request id, assigned pool id, region, and status codes. We will redact any PII.

3) Private/VPC: Because network connectivity and some key management controls are customer-controlled, Redwood's SOC 2 cannot assert implementation of those controls unless BrightGuard elected to include their VPC topology in our auditor's scope. For convenience, I've populated a checklist in the attached draft_bridge_letter_brightguard_v1.docx that BrightGuard can use to attest the items they control; once signed, our auditors will evaluate whether that evidence can permit an extension of coverage retroactively or for the subsequent audit period (depends on auditor acceptance).

Next steps I propose:
- We share the CAIQ matrix + draft bridge letter (attached).
- Schedule a 30-minute call to walk the BrightGuard audit team through the evidence mappings (Irene / Kimberly + Ben). Proposed times: 2026-09-06 10:00-10:30 PT or 2026-09-07 14:00-14:30 PT.

Attachments: draft_bridge_letter_brightguard_v1.docx

Ben Carter
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightguard.com>

Thanks — that was exactly what we needed. The CAIQ matrix and draft bridge letter look good at a glance. We'll review the sample log formats and get internal sign-off on the attestation checklist.

Please hold 2026-09-07 14:00 PT for the call (preferred). I'll send a calendar invite and include two auditors from my team. If we need the full 1% hashed-request sample earlier, we'll flag that in the invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maria Lopez

BrightGuard Financial
